title: NVMe overheating: every bd run rewrites its Dolt DB; server polled it (9.5 MB/s idle). Fixed by fingerprinting repos
close_reason: fixed: repos fingerprinted, bd no longer polled (9.5 MB/s -> noise floor)

title: Journal unreadable after a transient full disk (torn line followed by more writes)
description:
Source: test report 2026-11-03, RELAI-TEAM MAJOR 1. Reproduced twice by the tester and again on 2026-11-04 with RLIMIT_FSIZE (partial write, same effect as ENOSPC).

Symptom: a write fails halfway (ENOSPC), leaving a line without a newline. Once space is back the same process keeps appending after it, giving `{"seq":4,"time":"202{"seq":4,...`. On restart the server refuses to start: `events.jsonl:4: invalid character 's' after object key:value pair`.

Cause: internal/store/store.go, `Log.Append` does not go back to the last valid offset after a failed `Write`/`Sync`. `Replay` only tolerates an invalid line in last position, and `truncateTornTail` only handles a missing final newline.

Fix: (1) on a failed write, truncate the file back to the offset before the attempt (or refuse every later write); do not advance `next`. (2) At startup, quarantine an invalid line (log a warning, keep going, copy it to a side file) instead of refusing to start.

Related variant: an invalid last line that ends with a newline is dropped silently at first start (a claim vanishes without trace), then one new event makes the next start fail (`events.jsonl:7`). Same fix, plus a warning.

Acceptance: a store test that fails a write halfway (RLIMIT_FSIZE or a failing writer), appends again, then reopens the log successfully with all acknowledged events present; a test for the invalid-line-with-newline variant that checks the warning. Update the spec "Server restarts with in-progress claims" if behaviour wording changes.

title: Two servers on one journal give two winners for the same item
description:
Source: test report 2026-11-03, RELAI-TEAM MAJOR 2. Reproduced 2026-11-04: a second `store.Open` on the same path succeeds, and `bob` and `carol` both get `seq 1` on the same item.

The README documents "single instance, do not run two servers on one log", but nothing enforces it, and the failure is silent (duplicate seq numbers, two holders).

Fix: take an exclusive `flock` (LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on events.jsonl or a `.lock` file in `Open`; fail with a clear message naming the data_dir. Release on `Close`. Consider Windows (no flock): document or use a build-tagged fallback.

Acceptance: a test that opens the same journal twice and expects the second to fail with a clear error; README line updated from "do not" to "the server refuses to".

title: Go toolchain: govulncheck reports 45 reachable standard-library vulnerabilities with Go 1.23.4
description:
Source: test report, A12. govulncheck v1.1.4: 45 reachable stdlib vulnerabilities with Go 1.23.4 (e.g. via http.Server.ListenAndServeTLS, x509.CertPool.AppendCertsFromPEM), plus 8 in imported packages and 16 in required modules not called. go.mod says `go 1.23` with no `toolchain` line, so it depends on the compiler used. The Dockerfile uses `golang:1.23`.

Fix: install the latest Go 1.23.x (or a newer release) at /opt, add a `toolchain` line to go.mod, pin the Dockerfile to the same version, run govulncheck again and record the result. Decision for the owner: stay on 1.23.x or move to a newer branch. Same applies to the RELAI repo (CI uses 1.23).

title: Journal replay ignores unknown event types and invalid trailing lines without a message
description:
Source: test report, minor 3. A mistyped event type (`item_clamed`) makes every claim vanish silently. Same for an invalid final line and duplicated `seq` values (accepted).

Fix: log a warning for each skipped or suspicious event (unknown type, duplicate seq, dropped line), with file:line. Keep the behaviour (do not refuse to start) but make it visible. Pairs with the quarantine work in the full-disk task.

Acceptance: tests that capture the log output for each of the three cases.

title: Config is too permissive: unknown fields, empty repos, tiny tokens, control characters
description:
Source: test report, minor 4.
- Unknown field accepted: a typo such as `claim_leas` is ignored and the lease stays at 8 h. Use `json.Decoder.DisallowUnknownFields`.
- `repos: []`, `null`, `[""]` start an empty server. Refuse or warn loudly.
- A 1-character token is accepted. Set a minimum length (the generated ones are 48 hex chars).
- Identity containing `\n` and ANSI sequences is accepted (log injection). Restrict to a safe character set, as `init` already does.
- `claim_lease: "1ns"` is accepted. Set a sane minimum.
- `relai-server init --repos /nonexistent/a` writes a config with a missing repo. Check the paths exist (warn at least).

Acceptance: extend the 33-case validation matrix (test report script cfgmatrix.py) into a Go table test with these cases.

title: MCP tool texts: unvalidated status/limit, unknown repo reported as "nothing available", lease end without date
description:
Source: test report, minor 10 and section 5. No model was misled in the 11 real-agent runs, but scripted tests show:
- `board_claim_next repo=nope` answers "No unclaimed, non-blocked item is available." An agent concludes "nothing left" instead of "unknown repo". Return an explicit "unknown repo" error.
- `board_items status=bogus` returns "0 items" with no error. Validate against the known statuses and list them in the error.
- `limit` negative, 0 or "x" is silently ignored. Validate.
- Lease end is shown as `04:57Z` with no date. Show the full UTC timestamp.
- `id: null` is treated as a request; JSON-RPC says it should be refused (cosmetic).
- Also from the real-agent run "vague": the agent claimed an item but did not say so. Not a tool bug; consider making the claim response text more explicit ("You now hold X").

Acceptance: tests for each, and the tool descriptions updated.

title: Two distinct repos with the same relai.yaml id: possible item-id collision (not tested)
description: Source: test report, "Soupçons" (not reproduced, not tested). Write the test first: two repos with the same `id`, check whether items collide, claims cross over, or startup refuses. Expected behaviour to decide: refuse at startup with a clear message naming both paths.

title: Graceful shutdown takes 10 s and exits 1 with an SSE subscriber connected
description:
Source: test report, minor 1. SIGTERM with one `curl -N .../events` open: 10.2 s, then `relai-server: context deadline exceeded`, exit code 1 (reproduced twice). `docker stop` (10 s default) then ends with SIGKILL.

Cause: cmd/relai-server/main.go, `hs.Shutdown` waits for the SSE streams. Fix: close the event hub (end all streams) before `Shutdown`. Package has 0% coverage: add a test around the shutdown path.

Acceptance: shutdown with an open subscriber finishes in under 1 s and exits 0.

title: Server listens only after the first full read: /healthz silent for 25-41 s with 300 repos
description:
Source: test report, minor 6. With 300 repos `/healthz` does not answer for 25 to 41 s at start and restart. A liveness probe (Docker healthcheck, orchestrator) could kill the process mid-start.

Fix: start listening first; serve `/healthz` immediately and have the data endpoints report "loading" (503 with Retry-After, or a `ready: false` field) until the first read is done.

Acceptance: `/healthz` answers within 1 s with the 300-repo fixture; data endpoints behave sanely while loading.

title: full_refresh_interval "0s" re-reads everything each cycle with no startup warning
description: Source: test report, minor 8. Measured: 3 repos every 5 s = 12 `bd` calls in 22 s, 32 MiB (about 1.4 MiB/s). Documented in the README ("Do not leave it on a laptop") but silent at startup. Log a warning when the value is 0 or below a threshold (e.g. under 1 minute), stating the write cost. Consider refusing values under a floor unless forced.

title: relai-mcp dies on a JSON-RPC line larger than 4 MiB
description:
Source: test report, minor 2. `bufio.Scanner: token too long`, exit 1, the client sees a broken pipe (internal/mcp/server.go:60, 4 MiB buffer). A 1.5 MiB line is handled cleanly (HTTP 431 relayed as isError).

Fix: read lines with a reader that can skip an oversized line, answer a JSON-RPC error (-32600/-32700) and keep serving; or document the limit.

Acceptance: test sending a 5 MiB line then a `ping`; the ping is answered.

title: First read of many repos writes ~99 MiB (one fsync per event)
description:
Source: test report, minor 5. Reading 280 repos (3,640 events, 800 KiB journal) writes about 99 MiB to disk, roughly 27 KiB per event, once per fresh journal. Each restart also re-reads all Beads repos (20 repos = 20 `bd` calls = about 63 MiB). Not sustained, but matters for the fragile NVMe (see the 2026-11-03 thermal incident).

Fix: add `Log.AppendBatch` that writes all creation events then does a single fsync; use it for the initial load and per-refresh diffs.

Acceptance: measured write volume for the 280-repo fixture (`awk '$3=="sda"{print $10*512}' /proc/diskstats` before/after) drops by an order of magnitude; the crash-safety test still passes.

title: Test gaps: cmd/relai-server and cmd/relai-mcp at 0% coverage, no partial-write or claim_next concurrency tests
